q: What do off-grid Ranchi brick kilns burn, and what is the cluster's CO2?
title: Ranchi brick kilns: coal, diesel, no grid
short: Grade B coal, plus a little generator diesel, because Ranchi's 200 or so kilns are not on the grid. A 15,000 brick a day kiln fires 31.5 lakh bricks on 788 t of coal and 1.1 kL of diesel. At India's coal factor the cluster's 157,600 t is about 277,000 t CO2 (estimate).
audience: Bull’s trench kiln owners around Ranchi and the Ranchi Brick Fields Owners Association

p: Almost every kiln is a fixed chimney Bull's trench kiln, firing hand moulded solid bricks from December to June, about 210 days. Bricks are 9½ x 4½ x 3 inch and about 3.6 kg, heavier than most north Indian clusters. A season's output sells as about 50% Class 1, 22% meeta, 22% Class 2, with 6% rejected.

sections.h: No electricity bill, one Scope 2 line fewer
p: With no grid connection, a generator pumps the moulding water and powers whatever else the kiln needs. That makes the kiln's footprint all Scope 1: coal and diesel. It also means there is no meter reading to lean on, so the diesel slips and the coal weighbridge slips are the whole record.

sections.h: Why 25 t per lakh, against 17 in Lucknow
ul: Heavier bricks: 3.6 kg here against about 3.0 kg there.
Poorer firing: TERI measured 1.69 MJ per kg of fired brick, against 1.38 in Lucknow and 1.1 to 1.2 for a well run kiln.
Closing that gap is worth roughly a third of the coal.

p: TERI printed 166,000 t CO2 for the cluster's coal, about 1.05 t per tonne. The 1.76 used here is India's national average for domestic coal. If your coal supplier gives a GCV test, use it: a lower grade coal burns more tonnes for the same heat, but each tonne carries less carbon.

sections.h: What TERI says to change first
ul: Feeding practice, about 10%: crushed coal, small charges every 20 minutes, one fireman.
Zigzag firing, a further 10% or so: 15,760 t of coal a year across the cluster.

example.title: One Ranchi kiln, a season (estimate)
lines: Coal: 788 t x 1.76 t CO2 = 1,387 t
Per lakh bricks: 1,390 / 31.5 = 44 t, or about 440 kg per 1,000 bricks
Cluster: 157,600 t coal x 1.76 = 277,380 t, plus 210 kL diesel = 555 t: about 277,900 t
example.note: Coal, diesel and output from TERI's Ranchi brick kiln profile. Coal at India's domestic average of 1.76 kg CO2 per kg; diesel at the IPCC 2006 default.

senseible: Senseible reads coal invoices by the kilogram and diesel slips by the litre into a season's Scope 1 total, coal at 1.76 kg CO2 per kg; dividing by bricks fired needs your own production count.
